title: The Weekend AI Engineer: Hassan El Mghari
talk_summary: A tour of Hassan El Mghari's weekend side projects (image tagging, QR codes, photo restoration, RoomGPT) with lessons aimed at solo builders launching MVPs fast. The advice is about shipping simple consumer apps with off-the-shelf APIs, free/open-source distribution, and polished UI — not about running multi-agent engineering organizations.

takeaways.technique: Use off-the-shelf APIs instead of fine-tuning/building models
takeaways.what_they_do: For MVPs he deliberately skips fine-tuning and custom models, calling a hosted model API directly (e.g. one call to GFPGAN for photo restore).

takeaways.technique: Down-scope to a shippable MVP, launch, then iterate
takeaways.what_they_do: He insists an idea must be describable in five words and buildable in one or two weekends; if it fails, pivot; if it works, double down.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you can't describe your idea to me in five words like it might not do great

takeaways.what_they_do: He batches intense work into one weekend per month rather than continuous effort, then relaxes for two or three weekends.
takeaways.evidence_quote: I work in Sprints so I'll take a single weekend and I'll just drop everything
